historical_references.reference: Hyder Ali was a renowned military leader and ruler of the Kingdom of Mysore in South India during the 18th century. He was converted to Islam late in life and adopted the name Hyder after the Islamic title 'Sultan al-Hydar' (Ruler of the Seas).
historical_references.context: Hyder Ali rose to prominence as a military commander under the rule of the Wodeyar kings of Mysore. He seized power in 1761 and ruled until his death in 1782, expanding the kingdom and facing numerous battles against the British East India Company.

historical_references.reference: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah was the last ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty in India, ruling from 1580 to 1612. He is known by the Islamic name 'Hyder Shah' or 'Hyder Quli'.
historical_references.context: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, also known as Hyder Shah, was the founder of the city of Hyderabad, which later became the capital city of the Nizam of Hyderabad. He was a patron of arts and culture and is known for his contributions to the development of the city.
